newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 lower Tuesday in a technical correction to Monday's strong run-up, traders said.

New York cocoa futures rose sharply Monday, bolstered by chart-driven speculative buying. September settled up $32 at $1,539 a tonne after ranging between $1,540 and $1,494. Second-month December rose the same to $1,588, while the back months gained $29.
Technically, traders said September has support at $1,520, with resistance seen at a chart gap between $1,561 and $1,570.

On the fundamental side, official Ivorian shipping data showed Ivory Coast cocoa bean exports fell to 21,841 tonnes in June from 34,966 tonnes in May as port deliveries remained slack after the main crop (Oct-April) season.
Cumulative exports for the first nine months of 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) totalled 940,742 tonnes against 1,005,461 in 1995/96 and 719,063 the year before.
In London, cocoa futures were firmer early Tuesday, but below session highs. At the midday break, benchmark September was up six stg, to 1,024 stg, after ranging narrowly from 1,028 to 1,022 stg.
